Title:
Character of the immune response in guinea pigs following immunization with brucellosis protective antigen
Title: Character of the immune response in guinea pigs following immunization with brucellosis protective antigen
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigated the immune response in guinea pigs immunized with brucella protective antigen.
Vaccine Formulation: The antigen was administered intravenously at doses of 0.6 mg and 2 mg.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of guinea pigs followed by detection of antigen in lymph nodes and spleen using fluorescent antibody method; measurement of humoral response and phagocytic activity of peritoneal macrophages.
Vaccine Efficacy: The 0.6 mg dose produced an earlier and more pronounced humoral effect compared to 2 mg; low doses enhanced phagocytic activity, while 2 mg dose disturbed carbohydrate metabolism in phagocytes negatively affecting their function.
Immune Response: Antigen detectable for 30 days in lymph nodes and spleen; low dose induced stronger phagocytic activity and better humoral response; high dose impaired phagocyte metabolism and function.

Title:

Title: Responses of cattle to two dosages of Brucella abortus strain RB51: serology, clearance and efficacy

Vaccine Formulation: Subcutaneous vaccination with 1.6 x 10(10) or 3.2 x 10(10) colony-forming units of strain RB51.

Title:
Safety and efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in captive pregnant elk
Title: Safety and efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in captive pregnant elk
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella abortus strain RB51 is a laboratory-derived rough mutant of virulent B. abortus strain 2308 used as a vaccine because it induces antibodies that do not react on standard brucellosis serologic tests.
Vaccine Formulation: Intramuscular vaccination with 1.03 x 10^10 CFU of strain RB51.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Fourteen captive pregnant elk were randomly divided into vaccinated and control groups; vaccinated elk received strain RB51 vaccine intramuscularly; both groups were challenged 40 days postvaccination with 9.8 x 10^6 CFU of B. abortus strain 2308 intraconjunctivally.
Vaccine Efficacy: Abortion occurred in all control elk and in five of seven vaccinated elk postchallenge; no statistically significant protection was observed (P = 0.23).
Immune Response: Vaccinated elk seroconverted postvaccination; antibodies to strain RB51 were detected by a modified dot-blot assay.

Title: Response of Bali cattle (Bos javanicus) to vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 in West Timor
Vaccine Introduction: A trial was conducted in two villages in Timor, Indonesia, including one with infected cattle and one without, to determine the serological response to vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 in Bali cattle.
Vaccine Formulation: Mature female cattle were immunised with low-dose strain 19 (2x10^8-6x10^8 CFU) and calves (6-12 months) with high-dose strain 19 (4x10^10-12x10^10 CFU); control groups received sterile vaccine diluent.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Serological response was monitored by measuring seroprevalence and mean titres using complement-fixation test (CFT) up to 24 months post-vaccination; comparison of reproductive outcomes between seropositive and seronegative animals in infected and non-infected villages.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccinated cattle showed highest seroprevalence and titres 3 months post-vaccination, which receded over time; 1% of vaccinated calves and 1.9% of vaccinated cows remained seropositive at 24 months; vaccinated animals showed protection as non-vaccinated seropositive animals had higher rates of abortion and stillbirth.
Immune Response: Induction of serological response demonstrated by complement-fixation test; seropositivity persisted in a small percentage of vaccinated animals up to 24 months.

Title: Human peripheral blood T cells, monocytes, and macrophages secrete macrophage inflammatory proteins 1alpha and 1beta following stimulation with heat-inactivated Brucella abortus
Lab Model or Cell: human peripheral blood mononuclear cells; human CD4(+) T cells; human CD8(+) T cells; elutriated monocytes; macrophages
Vaccine Introduction: Heat-killed Brucella abortus (HBa) has been proposed as a carrier for therapeutic vaccines for individuals with immunodeficiency due to its ability to induce IL-2 and IFN-gamma in T cells and to upregulate antigen-presenting cell functions including IL-12 production.
Vaccine Formulation: Heat-killed Brucella abortus (HBa) and lipopolysaccharide isolated from HBa (LPS-Ba) were used to stimulate immune cells.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, purified T cells, elutriated monocytes, and macrophages with HBa or LPS-Ba; measurement of beta-chemokine secretion and mRNA expression; intracellular staining for IFN-gamma and MIP-1beta; assessment of CCR5-dependent HIV-1 envelope-mediated cell fusion inhibition.
Vaccine Efficacy: HBa and LPS-Ba stimulated secretion of beta-chemokines (MIP-1alpha and MIP-1beta) sufficient to block CCR5-dependent HIV-1 envelope-mediated cell fusion, suggesting antiviral activity.
Immune Response: Induction of IL-2 and IFN-gamma in CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cells; secretion of MIP-1alpha and MIP-1beta primarily by CD8(+) T cells, monocytes, and macrophages; upregulation of beta-chemokine mRNA within 30 minutes and protein secretion within 4 hours; beta-chemokine production not blocked by anti-IFN-gamma antibodies; majority of beta-chemokine-producing CD8(+) T cells also produced IFN-gamma.

Title: Lymphoblastic transformation by fractions of Brucella in patients having had brucellosis and subjects vaccinated by the vaccine PI
Vaccine Introduction: Two fractions of Brucella (P.I. and 4A) previously examined for vaccinal properties were used to study cellular immunity in brucellosis and to deduce a valid protection test.

Title:
Comparative behaviour of Brucella abortus strains 19 and RB51 in the pregnant mouse
Title: Comparative behaviour of Brucella abortus strains 19 and RB51 in the pregnant mouse
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine strain RB51, a stable rough organism, was administered intraperitoneally to pregnant mice to compare its pathogenicity with strain 19.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated rough strain RB51 organisms administered intraperitoneally at doses up to 10^9.5.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Pregnant BALB/c mice were inoculated on day 9 of gestation; nine days later, spleens and placentas were collected for bacteriological and histopathological examination; serological response was assessed by standard tube agglutination test.
Vaccine Efficacy: Strain RB51 produced mild to minimal placentitis without fetal death and resulted in a 10-fold lower splenic infection level compared to strain 19 at higher doses.
Immune Response: Mice infected with strain RB51 remained seronegative in the standard tube agglutination test, contrasting with seroconversion seen in strain 19 infected mice.

Title: Brucella lumazine synthase elicits a mixed Th1-Th2 immune response and reduces infection in mice challenged with Brucella abortus 544 independently of the adjuvant formulation used
Extracted Vaccine Name: recombinant lumazine synthase from Brucella spp.
Make Vaccine Name: recombinant lumazine synthase from Brucella spp.
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
Adjuvant: yes; aluminum hydroxide gel; monophosphoryl lipid A; incomplete Freund's adjuvant
Vaccine Introduction: The immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (rBLS) was evaluated in mice.
Vaccine Formulation: rBLS was administered alone or with aluminum hydroxide gel (BLS-Al), monophosphoryl lipid A (BLS-MPA), or incomplete Freund's adjuvant (BLS-IFA).

Vaccine Introduction: This prospective phase IV study involved vaccination of professionally exposed subjects who were negative to an intradermal test for previous contamination.

Title:

Title: Antibody response and antigen-specific gamma-interferon profiles of vaccinated and unvaccinated pregnant sheep experimentally infected with Brucella melitensis
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was used for prior immunization of pregnant ewes to protect against clinical brucellosis caused by experimental infection with Brucella melitensis.

Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccinated ewes did not contract clinical brucellosis nor excrete the pathogen, indicating protection against disease; non-vaccinated ewes showed classical brucellosis symptoms and pathogen excretion.
Immune Response: Vaccinated ewes showed low levels of circulating antibodies and antigen-specific gamma-interferon compared to non-vaccinated infected ewes, which had notably high antibody levels and gamma-IFN responses; high antibody and gamma-IFN levels correlated with active infection; protection by vaccination was associated with a low detectable immune response.

Title: Systemic and mucosal immunity in rhesus macaques immunized with HIV-1 peptide and gp120 conjugated to Brucella abortus

Title: Evaluation of cell-mediated immune responses and bacterial clearance in 6-10 months old water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) experimentally vaccinated with four dosages of commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine
Lab Model or Cell: peripheral blood mononuclear cells; lymph node mononuclear cells
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated cell-mediated immune responses and bacterial clearance in water buffalo vaccinated with different dosages of commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine.

Title: Conjunctival vaccination of pregnant ewes and goats with Brucella melitensis Rev 1 vaccine: safety and serological responses

Title:
Serologic responses, biosafety and clearance of four dosages of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in 6-10 months old water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)
Title: Serologic responses, biosafety and clearance of four dosages of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in 6-10 months old water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated antibody responses, bacterial clearance, and safety of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in water buffalo using four different dosages and vaccination schedules.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine administered in recommended dose and double dose, given once or twice 4 weeks apart.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Thirty water buffalo from a brucellosis-free farm were divided into five groups receiving different dosages and schedules of RB51 vaccine or saline control; antibody responses were monitored by complement fixation test and dot-blot assay; bacterial clearance was assessed from prescapular lymph nodes; shedding was evaluated by swabs from nasal, conjunctival, vaginal or preputial sites; serological tests for field strain B. abortus were performed.
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody responses to RB51 were demonstrated in all vaccinated groups up to 12 weeks post-inoculation; RB51 was cleared from lymph nodes between 6 and 12 weeks post-inoculation depending on dosage and schedule; no shedding of RB51 was detected; no interference with sero-surveillance for field strain B. abortus was observed.
Immune Response: Serologic responses to RB51 vaccination were detected by complement fixation test and dot-blot assay with 83.7% agreement; no serological evidence of field strain B. abortus infection was found in vaccinated or control animals.

Vaccine Introduction: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a divalent fusion DNA vaccine encoding both the Brucella abortus L7/L12 protein and Omp16 protein.

Title:
Efficacy of strain RB51 vaccine in heifers against experimental brucellosis
Title: Efficacy of strain RB51 vaccine in heifers against experimental brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of the rough Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in heifers as an additional tool for controlling bovine brucellosis in Brazil and to assess the full calf dose in adult cattle.
Vaccine Formulation: The vaccine was administered subcutaneously at doses of 1.5x10^10 CFU at Day 0 or 1.6x10^10 CFU at 60 days of gestation.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Thirty-three heifers (~24 months old) were divided into vaccinated (n=20) and control (n=13) groups. Vaccinated animals were challenged between 6 and 7 months of pregnancy with 3x10^8 CFU of virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308 via the conjunctival route. Serological tests (RBPAT, STAT, 2ME) were used to measure antibody response.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination prevented 59.4% of abortions, 58.6% of cow infections, and 61.0% of fetal infections. The cumulative incidence of abortions was 25% in vaccinated versus 62% in controls. Non-vaccinated animals had 2.462 times higher risk of abortion than vaccinated animals.
Immune Response: Vaccination with RB51 did not induce antibodies against the O-side chain of lipopolysaccharide as measured by conventional serological tests. No RB51 strain was isolated from samples, and no abortions were caused by vaccination at 60 days of pregnancy.

Title: Assessment of serological response of young and adult sheep to conjunctival vaccination with Rev-1 vaccine by fluorescence polarization assay (FPA) and other serological tests for B. melitensis
Vaccine Introduction: The study assessed the serological response of young and adult sheep vaccinated conjunctivally with the Rev-1 vaccine.
Vaccine Formulation: Conjunctival administration of the live attenuated Rev-1 vaccine.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Serological tests including fluorescence polarization assay (FPA), Rose Bengal test (RBT), complement fixation test (CFT), modified Rose Bengal test (m-RBT), indirect ELISA (i-ELISA), and competitive ELISA (c-ELISA) were used to monitor antibody responses at multiple time points post vaccination in 136 adult sheep and 64 lambs.
Vaccine Efficacy: Not directly reported; the study focused on serological responses and test performance rather than protective efficacy.
Immune Response: Most animals showed positive serological reactions by FPA, RBT, CFT, m-RBT, and c-ELISA at 21 days post vaccination; i-ELISA positivity appeared at 42 days. Tests performed equally well at 4 months post vaccination in lambs and at 8 months in adults for FPA, RBT, CFT, and c-ELISA. i-ELISA and m-RBT showed low specificity in adults at 11 months post vaccination. The study suggests that vaccinated lambs can be accurately tested by any diagnostic test at least 4 months post vaccination, but m-RBT and i-ELISA are not recommended for adult testing at 11 months due to low specificity.

Title:

Title: Parenteral vaccination of domestic pigs with Brucella abortus strain RB51
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to determine the immunogenicity and efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 as a vaccine in domestic pigs.
Vaccine Formulation: Parenteral (intramuscular) vaccination with 2 x 10^10 CFUs of strain RB51.

Title:

Title: Immune responses of elk to initial and booster vaccinations with Brucella abortus strain RB51 or 19
Vaccine Introduction: Elk were vaccinated with 10^10 CFU of strain RB51 and booster vaccinated with a similar dosage at 65 weeks.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 culture at 10^10 CFU dose.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunologic responses were characterized by measuring antibody responses, proliferative responses to autologous and nonautologous antigens, gamma interferon production, and flow cytometric analysis of lymphocyte subsets after initial and booster vaccination in elk.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination induced greater antibody responses compared to controls; proliferative responses to autologous antigen were significant at some time points after initial vaccination but generally transient; booster vaccination did not elicit strong anamnestic cellular responses; overall immune responses were less robust than in cattle or bison, suggesting poor protection in elk.
Immune Response: Increased antibody responses after initial and booster vaccination; transient proliferative responses mainly in IgM-positive cells; limited CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proliferation detected only at 22 weeks post initial vaccination; no significant gamma interferon production differences after booster; weak or absent anamnestic cellular responses after booster.

Title: Effects of stage of gestation and breed on bovine responses to vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Eighty-eight cattle were injected subcutaneously with 2.5 x 10^8 viable cells of Brucella abortus strain 19.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated whole organism vaccine containing viable Brucella abortus strain 19 cells.

Vaccine Efficacy: All but one heifer became seropositive; seropositivity decreased over time; seropositivity varied by stage of gestation at vaccination; no brucellosis-positive results in nonpregnant heifers; no relation of breed or calf survival to brucellosis-positive results; cultures from milk and tissues were negative for B. abortus.
Immune Response: Induction of seropositivity detected by multiple serologic tests; proportion positive varied by test type and stage of gestation; serologic classification identified some reactors and suspects.

Title: Partial protection against Brucella infection in mice by immunization with nonpathogenic alphaproteobacteria
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus NPAP live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Type: VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine; VO:0010008: inactivated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Immunization with nonpathogenic alphaproteobacteria (NPAP) such as Ochrobactrum anthropi, Sinorhizobium meliloti, Mesorhizobium loti, and Agrobacterium tumefaciens was hypothesized to protect mice from Brucella infection due to cross-recognition of antigens.
Vaccine Formulation: Heat-killed NPAP bacteria or cytosoluble extracts from NPAP or Brucella abortus were used; live NPAP were also used for oral immunization.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Mice were immunized subcutaneously or intraperitoneally with heat-killed NPAP or cytosoluble extracts, or orally with live NPAP, then challenged intravenously or orally with Brucella abortus 2308; serum and fecal antibody responses and splenic CFU counts were measured.
Vaccine Efficacy: Partial protection was observed with NPAP immunization, with significant reductions in splenic CFU counts compared to controls; protection levels varied by NPAP species and immunization route but were lower than those conferred by Brucella melitensis H38 or heat-killed B. abortus.
Immune Response: Immunization induced cross-reacting serum antibodies against Brucella antigens; oral immunization with NPAP increased serum IgG and, after challenge, serum and fecal IgA against Brucella antigens, especially with O. anthropi.

Title:
Protection of mice from Brucella infection by immunization with attenuated Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium expressing A L7/L12 and BLS fusion antigen of Brucella
Title: Protection of mice from Brucella infection by immunization with attenuated Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium expressing A L7/L12 and BLS fusion antigen of Brucella
Vaccine Type: VO:0000624: subunit vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine; VO:0000636: recombinant vector vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study describes the use of attenuated Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium strains expressing a L7/L12 and BLS fusion antigen of Brucella as a vaccination strategy to prevent Brucella infection in mice.
Vaccine Formulation: Two attenuated S. typhimurium strains carrying plasmids expressing the fusion antigen were used: X4072bl delivering antigen expressed by the bacterium itself, and X4550bl delivering antigen to be expressed in target eukaryotic cells; also compared with recombinant BLS-L7/L12 fusion protein vaccine (rBL) and pVAX1-BLS-L7/L12 DNA vaccine (pBL).
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Oral administration of attenuated Salmonella strains to BALB/c mice; comparison with intramuscular injection of recombinant protein and DNA vaccines; assessment of mucosal and systemic immunity and protection against B. abortus 544 infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: Both attenuated Salmonella carrier strains elicited mucosal and systemic immunity and induced protection against B. abortus 544 infection; recombinant protein and DNA vaccines induced humoral and cellular responses but not mucosal immunity and provided lower protection.
Immune Response: Oral Salmonella-based vaccines induced mucosal and systemic immunity; recombinant protein and DNA vaccines induced humoral and cellular immune responses but lacked mucosal immunity.

Title:

Title: Construction of BP26 tagged vaccine strain and development of discriminating PCR for Brucella
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella strain M5 delta BP26 live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to modify the live attenuated vaccine strain M5 by deleting the BP26 gene to overcome drawbacks such as residual virulence, similar antigenicity to virulent strains, and difficulty in differentiating vaccination from natural infection.
Vaccine Formulation: A tagged vaccine strain M5DeltaBP26 was constructed by replacing the BP26 gene with a kanamycin resistance gene using homologous recombination.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Intracellular survival capability of M5DeltaBP26 and wild type strain M5 was compared in macrophages and mice. A duplex PCR was developed based on dnaK and BP26 deletion sequences to differentiate M5DeltaBP26 from wild type and virulent strains.
Vaccine Efficacy: M5DeltaBP26 showed decreased infection capability compared to M5 in mice, with significantly lower CFU counts at 2 and 3 weeks post-infection, indicating reduced virulence.

Title: Immune responses and efficacy after administration of a commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to cattle
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the immunologic responses and efficacy of a commercially available Brucella abortus strain RB51 (SRB51) live vaccine to protect cattle against brucellosis.
Vaccine Formulation: Commercially available SRB51 vaccine administered subcutaneously at doses of 10^9 or 10^10 CFU.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Pregnant Hereford heifers were vaccinated and then challenged intraconjunctivally at 180 days gestation with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308. Serologic responses were monitored by standard tube agglutination test and dot-blot assay. Peripheral blood mononuclear cell proliferative responses to gamma-irradiated SRB51 were also assessed.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination with 10^10 CFU SRB51 was highly efficacious (P < .02) in preventing Brucella-induced abortion or fetal infection. Vaccinated cattle had significantly fewer abortions and reduced fetal infection compared to nonvaccinates. However, incidence of maternal infection at necropsy did not differ significantly between vaccinated and nonvaccinated groups.
Immune Response: Vaccinated cattle showed greater antibody responses to SRB51 at 4 and 8 weeks post-vaccination and greater lymphocyte proliferative responses at 10, 12, 14, and 16 weeks compared to nonvaccinates.

Title: The protein moiety of Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 16 is a new bacterial pathogen-associated molecular pattern that activates dendritic cells in vivo, induces a Th1 immune response, and is a promising self-adjuvanting vaccine against systemic and oral acquired brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The study hypothesized that Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 16 lipoprotein could elicit a protective immune response without external adjuvants. The protein portion of Omp16 (unlipidated Omp16) was tested for protective efficacy.
Vaccine Formulation: Unlipidated Omp16 protein administered intraperitoneally and orally; also plant-expressed recombinant U-Omp16 for oral delivery.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Protection against B. abortus infection was evaluated after intraperitoneal and oral immunization; dendritic cell activation was assessed in vivo and in vitro; TLR4 dependency was investigated.

Immune Response: U-Omp16 induced a Th1-specific immune response; activated dendritic cells and macrophages in vitro and in vivo; the immune response and protection were TLR4 dependent; U-Omp16 exhibited self-adjuvanting properties including mucosal adjuvanticity.

Title: Vaccination strategies for managing brucellosis in Yellowstone bison
Vaccine Introduction: Concerns over migratory bison transmitting brucellosis to cattle led to proposals for bison vaccination.

Title:

Title: Immune responses and protection against experimental Brucella suis biovar 1 challenge in nonvaccinated or B. abortus strain RB51-vaccinated cattle
Vaccine Introduction: Twenty Hereford heifers approximately 9 months old were vaccinated with 2 × 10^10 CFU of the RB51 vaccine or saline as control.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine administered at 2 × 10^10 CFU.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunologic responses measured by antibody and lymphocyte proliferative responses; pregnant cattle challenged conjunctivally with 10^7 CFU of Brucella suis biovar 1; serologic tests including fluorescence polarization assay and buffered acid plate agglutination test used to detect infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination with RB51 did not reduce Brucella suis infection rates in maternal or fetal tissues; no abortions occurred in either vaccinated or control groups; increased incidence of retained placenta observed in both groups; RB51 vaccination did not protect cattle against B. suis infection after exposure.
Immune Response: RB51-vaccinated cattle showed significantly greater antibody and proliferative responses to RB51 antigens compared to controls; however, serologic and lymphocyte proliferative responses to B. suis antigens did not differ between vaccinated and control cattle after experimental infection.

Title:
Effectiveness of Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide as an adjuvant for tuberculin PPD
Title: Effectiveness of Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide as an adjuvant for tuberculin PPD
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella abortus LPS was evaluated for its immunostimulatory properties as an adjuvant due to its lower toxicity and lack of pyrogenic properties compared to other bacterial LPS.
Vaccine Formulation: B. abortus LPS was used as an adjuvant combined with tuberculin purified protein derivative (PPD) fractions (17th and 23rd) and BCG in immunization experiments.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: BALB/c mice were immunized with antigen preparations (BCG, PPD, 17th and 23rd PPD fractions) combined with either complete Freund's adjuvant or B. abortus LPS; immune responses were assessed by measuring Th1-type cytokine (IFN-γ), Th2-type cytokines (IL-5, IL-10), and specific IgG levels.
Vaccine Efficacy: Immunization with the 17th PPD fraction plus B. abortus LPS induced a Th1-type cytokine response with a high IFN-γ/IL-5 ratio; immunization with PPD or 23rd PPD fraction plus B. abortus LPS resulted in a mixed Th1/Th2 cytokine response.
Immune Response: The 17th PPD fraction with B. abortus LPS adjuvant elicited a Th1-biased immune response characterized by elevated IFN-γ relative to IL-5, indicating enhanced cell-mediated immunity; other fractions induced mixed Th1/Th2 responses.

Title:
Effect of dose of Brucella abortus strain 19 in yearling heifers on the relative risk of developing brucellosis from challenge exposure with strain 2308
Title: Effect of dose of Brucella abortus strain 19 in yearling heifers on the relative risk of developing brucellosis from challenge exposure with strain 2308
Vaccine Introduction: Yearling heifers were vaccinated subcutaneously with different doses (10^8, 10^9, 10^10 CFU) of Brucella abortus strain 19.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 culture at varying doses.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Vaccinated heifers were challenged 9 months post-vaccination with 10^7 CFU of Brucella abortus strain 2308; serologic tests and lymphocyte transformation assays were performed; tissue specimens were cultured at parturition and necropsy.
Vaccine Efficacy: Relative risk of developing brucellosis was reduced dose-dependently to 0.38, 0.15, and 0.06 for doses 10^8, 10^9, and 10^10 CFU respectively compared to controls.
Immune Response: Serologic positivity increased with dose initially but declined by 4 months; ELISA positivity persisted beyond 4 months but was negative by 9 months; lymphocyte transformation activity was comparable for 10^9 and 10^10 doses with about half of heifers showing positive stimulation index at 9 months.

Title:

Title: Protective live oral brucellosis vaccines stimulate Th1 and th17 cell responses
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis znuA deletion live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine is a live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain with deletion of the znuA gene involved in zinc transport, developed to provide protection against inhalational infection.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated ΔznuA B. melitensis administered orally.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Oral vaccination of mice followed by nasal challenge with wild-type Brucella melitensis 16M; evaluation of bacterial clearance in spleens and lungs; use of gamma interferon-deficient mice to assess immune response dependency; measurement of cytokine responses including IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-22.

Title: Evaluation of the recombinant 10-kilodalton immunodominant region of the BP26 protein of Brucella abortus for specific diagnosis of bovine brucellosis

Immune Response: Not reported (study focused on diagnostic antigen evaluation rather than immunization or immune response).

Title: Tandem repeats of the extracellular domain of Matrix 2 influenza protein exposed in Brucella lumazine synthase decameric carrier molecule induce protection in mice

Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit vaccine carrying Matrix 2 extracellular domain
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated Brucella abortus lumazine synthase (BLS), a highly immunogenic decameric protein, as a carrier for the influenza Matrix 2 extracellular domain (M2e) peptide, aiming to develop a broadly protective influenza vaccine.
Vaccine Formulation: Chimeric proteins were generated by fusing one or four tandem copies of M2e to BLS, expressed in Escherichia coli, and assembled into decameric subunits exposing M2e peptides at the N-terminal ends; formulations included adjuvants such as Iscomatrix and alum.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of mice with purified chimeric proteins carrying one or four M2e copies, with or without adjuvants, followed by challenge with live influenza virus to assess protection.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination with BLS-4M2e plus Iscomatrix adjuvant resulted in 100% survival; with alum adjuvant, 80% survival; BLS-4M2e alone protected 60% of mice; all results statistically significant compared to controls.
Immune Response: Immunization elicited significant humoral immune responses; fusion of four tandem M2e copies induced similar antibody levels without adjuvant, while one M2e copy required adjuvants for significant response.

Title: Serological and allergic reactions of ewes after simultaneous vaccinations with two living attenuated strains of Brucella and Salmonella
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was administered to 4-6-month-old ewe-lambs either subcutaneously or conjunctivally.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Vaccination of ewe-lambs with Rev. 1 vaccine alone or simultaneously with Salmonella abortusovis strain Rv6 vaccine; serological tests (complement fixation test, Rose Bengal plate test), allergic intrapalpebral reaction to brucellin.
Vaccine Efficacy: Serological and allergic responses to Rev. 1 vaccine were demonstrated; serological reactions remained positive in about 10% of subcutaneously vaccinated ewes and negative in all conjunctivally vaccinated ewes at 6 months post-vaccination.
Immune Response: Allergic responses to Rev. 1 vaccine were lower after conjunctival vaccination than subcutaneous injection; simultaneous vaccination with Rv6 decreased allergic responses in subcutaneously vaccinated ewes but did not interfere with serological or allergic responses to Rev. 1 vaccine one month after vaccination.

Title: Protection of mice against Shiga toxin 2 (Stx2)-associated damage by maternal immunization with a Brucella lumazine synthase-Stx2 B subunit chimera
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella lumazine synthase-Stx2 B subunit chimera
Make Vaccine Name: Brucella lumazine synthase-Stx2 B subunit chimera
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella lumazine synthase Stx2 B subunit subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: A novel immunogen was developed based on the B subunit of Shiga toxin 2 (Stx2B) and the enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) to protect against Stx2-associated damage.
Vaccine Formulation: Chimeric protein combining Brucella lumazine synthase and Shiga toxin 2 B subunit.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Maternal immunization of BALB/c female mice with BLS-Stx2B before mating; measurement of antibody titers in dams and pups; lethal systemic Stx2 injection challenge; oral challenge with Stx2-producing EHEC strain; fostering experiments to assess antibody transfer via breast-feeding; subsequent intravenous Stx2 challenge in pups.
Vaccine Efficacy: Pups born to immunized dams showed comparable anti-Stx2B antibody titers, were totally protected against lethal systemic Stx2 injection up to 2-3 months postpartum, resisted oral EHEC challenge without symptoms, and survived subsequent intravenous Stx2 challenge due to prolonged active immunity.
Immune Response: Maternal immunization induced anti-Stx2B neutralizing IgG antibodies transmitted through breast-feeding; pups developed active and specific immune responses after surviving EHEC infection.

Title: Immunity to Brucella abortus induced in mice by popliteal lymph node restricted strain 19 vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was administered by footpad injection in mice, leading to colonization of the popliteal lymph node and spleen for at least 15 days before progressive disappearance.

Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Colonization studies in mice; immune serum administration to restrict colonization; virulent challenge spleen count method to measure immunity at 90 and 180 days post-vaccination; comparison of lymph node restricted versus systemic vaccination.

Immune Response: Restricted vaccination mainly triggered the T-cell limb of immunity; systemic vaccination triggered both humoral and cellular effectors.

Vaccine Introduction: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding ribosomal protein L9 of Brucella abortus (pVaxL9) was generated to evaluate its immunogenicity and protective efficacy.

Title:
Oral delivery of Brucella spp. recombinant protein U-Omp16 abrogates the IgE-mediated milk allergy
Title: Oral delivery of Brucella spp. recombinant protein U-Omp16 abrogates the IgE-mediated milk allergy
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to examine the capacity of the unlipidated outer membrane protein 16 kDa (U-Omp16) from Brucella abortus to abrogate allergen-specific Th2 immune response when administered orally as an adjuvant in a mouse model of food allergy.
Vaccine Formulation: Oral administration of recombinant U-Omp16 protein combined with cow's milk proteins (CMP) during sensitization.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Balb/c mice were sensitized with cholera toxin and CMP by gavage and simultaneously treated with U-Omp16 and CMP; oral challenge with CMP was performed; allergic symptoms, skin tests, local small bowel cytokine and transcription factor gene expression, serum specific isotypes, and spleen cell-secreted cytokines were evaluated.
Vaccine Efficacy: Oral administration of U-Omp16 with CMP during sensitization reduced allergic symptoms, resulted in negative immediate skin test, increased skin delayed-type hypersensitivity response, inhibited serum specific IgE and IL-5, and promoted a Th1 immune response.
Immune Response: Shift from Th2 to Th1 predominance evidenced by increased specific IgG2a antibodies, CMP-induced IFN-γ secretion, inhibition of IL-13 and Gata-3 gene expression, and induction of IFN-γ and T-bet at the mucosal site.

Title:
Immunization with Brucella VirB proteins reduces organ colonization in mice through a Th1-type immune response and elicits a similar immune response in dogs
Title: Immunization with Brucella VirB proteins reduces organ colonization in mice through a Th1-type immune response and elicits a similar immune response in dogs
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine targets VirB7, a component of the type IV secretion system, a key virulence factor mediating intracellular survival of Brucella spp.
Vaccine Formulation: VirB7 protein administered subcutaneously in three doses with QuilA adjuvant.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of mice and dogs followed by in vitro splenocyte and PBMC stimulation assays, intraperitoneal challenge with live Brucella abortus in mice, skin test for delayed-type hypersensitivity in dogs, and in vitro complement-dependent bacteriolysis assay using sera from immunized dogs.
Vaccine Efficacy: Mice immunized with VirB7 showed almost 1 log reduction in spleen bacterial load after challenge with live Brucella abortus compared to unvaccinated controls; sera from immunized dogs mediated significant bacteriolysis of B. canis in vitro.
Immune Response: Immunized mice splenocytes produced significant and specific IFN-γ without IL-4, indicating a Th1-type response; immunized dogs’ PBMCs produced significantly higher IFN-γ upon stimulation; positive delayed-type hypersensitivity skin test in most immunized dogs; anti-VirB7 antibodies mediated complement-dependent bacteriolysis.

Title: Immune Response of Calves Vaccinated with Brucella abortus S19 or RB51 and Revaccinated with RB51

Immune Response: Strong and complex Th1 immune response characterized by T-cell proliferation, cytokine production, memory cell induction, and antibody production; after RB51 revaccination, increased IFN-ɣ expression, antigen-specific T-cell proliferation, cytotoxic CD8+ T-cells, and decreased IL-6 production; CD4+-dominant polarization after booster in S19 prime-vaccinated animals.

Title: Simultaneous immunization of mice with Omp31 and TF provides protection against Brucella melitensis infection
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 and trigger factor subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Subunit vaccines were developed using recombinant outer membrane protein Omp31 and trigger factor chaperone protein (TF) of Brucella melitensis, administered alone or in combination, as safer alternatives to live attenuated vaccines.
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant proteins rOmp31 and rTF used alone or combined as a cocktail.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of BALB/c mice followed by measurement of antigen-specific antibody titers (IgG1, IgG2a), lymphocyte proliferation, cytokine expression (IFN-γ, IL-12, IL-10, IL-6), CD4 and CD8 T cell levels, and protection against Brucella melitensis infection compared to Rev. 1 vaccine strain.

Immune Response: Immunized mice showed strong antigen-specific antibody responses (IgG1 and IgG2a), robust lymphocyte proliferation, elevated cytokine production (IFN-γ, IL-12, IL-10, IL-6), and increased CD4 and CD8 T cell frequencies; combination vaccine induced slightly higher immune parameters than single antigen vaccines.

Title: Serological diagnostic potential of recombinant outer membrane proteins (rOMPs) from Brucella melitensis in mouse model using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
Make Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis OMP25; OMP28; OMP31 vaccine
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis OMP25, OMP28, OMP31 subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to develop an indirect ELISA diagnostic assay using a combination of recombinant outer membrane proteins (rOMP25, rOMP28, rOMP31) from Brucella melitensis to improve serological diagnosis of brucellosis and reduce false positive serological reactions caused by smooth lipopolysaccharides (S-LPS).
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant OMP25, OMP28, and OMP31 proteins were cloned and expressed using a prokaryotic pET-32 Ek/LIC system and combined as one coating antigen for the indirect ELISA.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Three groups of BALB/c mice were used: group 1 infected with B. melitensis strain 0331 field strain; group 2 injected with B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine strain; group 3 infected with Yersinia enterocolitica O:9. Antibody responses were measured by Rose Bengal plate test (RBPT) and the developed rOMPs indirect ELISA.
Vaccine Efficacy: The rOMPs I-ELISA showed 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in differentiating mice infected with B. melitensis strain 0331 from vaccinated mice and mice infected with Y. enterocolitica O:9, whereas RBPT failed to differentiate these groups.
Immune Response: Western immunoblotting confirmed reactivity of the recombinant proteins; the rOMPs I-ELISA detected specific antibody responses in infected mice, demonstrating its potential to differentiate false positive serological reactions in brucellosis diagnosis.

Title: Intraperitoneal administration of a novel chimeric immunogen (rOP) elicits IFN-γ and IL-12p70 protective immune response in BALB/c mice against virulent Brucella

Title: Comparative experimental study of Brucella melitensis and its lipopolysaccharide in mouse model infected via subcutaneous route of exposure
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigated the immunopathophysiological aspects of Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide as a potential vaccine component by subcutaneous inoculation in a mouse model.
Vaccine Formulation: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) isolated from Brucella melitensis was administered subcutaneously at a dose of 0.4 mL containing 10^9 units.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: BALB/c mice were subcutaneously inoculated with LPS and monitored for clinical signs, hematological and histopathological changes, cytokine and antibody responses, and hormone levels over 24 days post-inoculation.
Vaccine Efficacy: LPS stimulated significant innate and acquired immune responses without causing significant systemic dysfunction, suggesting potential protective properties as an alternative vaccine for brucellosis.
Immune Response: Elevated levels of interleukins IL-1β and IL-6, and antibody levels IgM and IgG were observed as early as 3 days post-infection, with predominance in the LPS-infected group.

Title: Abortions in an organized dairy farm from North India reveal the possibility of breed susceptibility to Bovine Brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was used as a calf-hood vaccination in all heifers in an organized dairy farm in North India.

Vaccine Efficacy: Despite vaccination with strain 19 vaccine, abortions suspected of bovine brucellosis occurred, with bacteriological isolation in 4 dams and PCR positivity in 24 dams; vaccine did not fully prevent infection or abortion in Frieswal and Crossbred breeds, while Sahiwal breed showed no positive cases.

Title: Vaccination of goats with a combination Salmonella vector expressing four Brucella antigens (BLS, PrpA, Omp19, and SOD) confers protection against Brucella abortus infection
Extracted Vaccine Name: combination Salmonella vector expressing four Brucella antigens (BLS, PrpA, Omp19, and SOD)
Make Vaccine Name: combination Salmonella vector expressing four Brucella antigens (BLS, PrpA, Omp19, and SOD)
Standardized Vaccine Name: Salmonella Typhimurium recombinant vector vaccine expressing Brucella abortus BLS PrpA Omp19 and SOD proteins
Vaccine Introduction: This study explores the efficacy of a Salmonella Typhimurium delivery-based combination vaccine expressing four heterologous Brucella antigens targeting brucellosis in goats.
Vaccine Formulation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS), proline racemase subunit A (PrpA), outer-membrane protein 19 (Omp19), and Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); administered subcutaneously at two inoculation levels (5 × 10^9 CFU/mL and 5 × 10^10 CFU/mL).
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of goats followed by challenge with virulent Brucella abortus at 6 weeks post-immunization; measurement of serum IgG titers, interferon-γ production from peripheral blood mononuclear cells, bacterial loads in tissues, relative real-time PCR for antigen expression, and histopathological lesion assessment.
Vaccine Efficacy: Immunized goats showed significantly higher protection demonstrated by lower bacterial loads in most tissues, reduced expression of Brucella antigens in spleen, kidney, and lung, and ameliorated histopathological lesions compared to non-immunized controls.
Immune Response: Significantly higher serum IgG titers against individual Brucella antigens and elevated interferon-γ production from peripheral blood mononuclear cells in vaccinated groups compared to non-immunized goats.

Evaluation of immunogenicity and protection conferred by intranasal and conjunctival immunization with BLSOmp31-ChM and BLSOmp31-P407-Ch in rams.

Induction of systemic, local, and preputial IgG and IgA antibodies; significant specific cellular immune responses; no interference with serological diagnosis.

Title: Immunomodulation with killed Propionibacterium acnes in guinea pigs simultaneously vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19

Title: Anti-Brucella immunity transferred by immune serum and that transferred by splenic lymphocytes cannot be added

Title: Nanoparticle or conventional adjuvants: which one improves immune response against Brucellosis?
Adjuvant: yes; Aluminum Hydroxide; Incomplete Freund; Chitosan Nanoparticle
Vaccine Introduction: Subunit vaccines are considered as an efficient strategy against Brucellosis but are usually less immunogenic than live or killed vaccines; the study aimed to find a proper adjuvant to enhance immune response.
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant OMP25 protein formulated with different adjuvants including Aluminum Hydroxide (AH), Incomplete Freund (IFA), Chitosan Nanoparticle (CS), and combinations of CS with AH or IFA.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of mice followed by measurement of cytokine responses (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-4), antibody titers (total antibody, IgG1, IgG2a), and antigen-specific cell proliferation assays.
Vaccine Efficacy: CS adjuvant stimulated higher IFN-γ immunity and higher total antibody titers; rOMP25 formulated with CS, IFA, and IFA-CS induced higher IgG2a titers; cell proliferation was promoted after immunization with CS; TNF-α levels were not significantly different except for single IFA treatment.
Immune Response: CS adjuvant induced a stronger Th1-type immune response (higher IFN-γ and IgG2a) and lower IL-4 response compared to other adjuvants; overall, CS alone or combined with IFA improved Th1-Th2 responses.

Title: Brucella melitensis Rev.1 vaccination generates a higher shedding risk of the vaccine strain in Alpine ibex (Capra ibex) compared to the domestic goat (Capra hircus)
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination was considered as a possible way to control Brucella infection in the wildlife population of Alpine ibex.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Twelve ibexes and twelve goats were allocated into four groups housed separately, each including six males or six non-pregnant females. Four to five animals were vaccinated and one or two animals were contact animals. Half of the animals were necropsied 45 days post-vaccination, and the remaining ones at 90 days post-vaccination. Additional samples were collected 20 and 68 days post-vaccination to explore bacterial distribution in organs and humoral immunity.
Vaccine Efficacy: All vaccinated animals seroconverted. No clinical signs or Brucella-specific lesions were observed. The proportion of infected samples was significantly higher in ibex compared to goats and decreased between 45 and 90 days post-vaccination. Two male ibex presented urogenital excretion at 20 or 45 days post-vaccination. Bacterial load was higher at 45 days in ibexes compared to goats, and remained moderate to low at 90 days post-vaccination in both species with large variability between animals.
Immune Response: All vaccinated animals seroconverted, indicating a humoral immune response. Antibody profiles were highly contrasted between ibex and goats.

Title: Vaccine Candidate Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR Is Safe in a Pregnant Sheep Model and Confers Protection
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis 16M delta vjbR live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine candidate Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR was evaluated for safety and efficacy in pregnant sheep, a natural host species, to address the limitations of the current live-attenuated vaccine Rev. 1 which causes abortions in pregnant animals.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR strain administered subcutaneously at 1 × 10^10 CFU/ml.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Pregnant sheep (n=6) were vaccinated subcutaneously at approximately 70 days gestation with 16MΔvjbR or Rev. 1. Safety was assessed by abortion rates, placental colonization, and vertical transmission evaluated by culture and histopathology of fetal tissues. Efficacy was tested by conjunctival challenge with 1 × 10^7 CFU/ml B. melitensis five weeks postpartum, followed by assessment of tissue colonization.
Vaccine Efficacy: 16MΔvjbR provided protection comparable to Rev. 1 with no statistical difference in colonization of target organs after challenge.
Immune Response: Not reported explicitly in the abstract.

Title:
Clinical results of an inactivated anti-brucella vaccine in combination with immunomodulators
Title: Clinical results of an inactivated anti-brucella vaccine in combination with immunomodulators
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to obtain a vaccine against animal brucellosis with high immunogenic properties by evaluating the effectiveness of a split-conjugated vaccine combined with immunomodulators fosprenil and polypeptide C.
Vaccine Formulation: The dry split-conjugated vaccine was dissolved in saline; fosprenil was administered intramuscularly; polypeptide C was mixed with the vaccine for subcutaneous injection in one group; another group received vaccine diluted with isotonic sodium chloride solution.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Eighteen Holstein Friesian calves were divided into three groups receiving different vaccine and immunomodulator combinations; serological tests (agglutination reaction, complement fixation, rose Bengal test) were performed on days 14, 30, and 90 post-vaccination.
Vaccine Efficacy: The split-conjugated vaccine combined with fosprenil induced higher antibody titers that persisted longer compared to the vaccine combined with polypeptide C or vaccine alone.
Immune Response: The vaccine with fosprenil enhanced the humoral immune response against brucellosis in calves.

Title: A safe non-toxic Brucella abortus ghosts induce immune responses and confer protection in BALB/c mice
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta gntR ghost live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to generate Brucella abortus ghosts by homologous recombination and bacterial ghost technologies to create a safe vaccine candidate.

Vaccine Efficacy: The 2308ΔgntR ghost induced high protective immunity against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain S2308 in BALB/c mice.
Immune Response: The vaccine elicited a strong anti-Brucella-specific IgG response, induced secretion of IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines, and stimulated robust spleen CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses.

Title:
Recombinant Lactococcus Lactis Displaying Omp31 Antigen of Brucella melitensis Can Induce an Immunogenic Response in BALB/c Mice
Title: Recombinant Lactococcus Lactis Displaying Omp31 Antigen of Brucella melitensis Can Induce an Immunogenic Response in BALB/c Mice
Make Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 recombinant vector vaccine
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 recombinant vector vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Since Brucella infection mostly occurs through mucosal surfaces, a vaccine delivered via mucosal route can enhance immune response to control brucellosis. Omp31 is a major outer membrane protein and protective antigen of Brucella.
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis displaying Omp31 antigen was constructed by fusing omp31 gene with usp45 signal peptide and M6 cell wall anchor in pNZ7021 expression vector; live and killed forms of recombinant L. lactis were used for oral and intraperitoneal immunization, respectively.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of BALB/c mice orally with live or intraperitoneally with killed recombinant L. lactis expressing Omp31; evaluation of humoral and cellular immune responses by measuring specific cytokines and antibodies.
Vaccine Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant increases in sIgA, serum IgA, IgM, and total IgG antibodies with live vaccine; killed vaccine induced significant increases in serum IgM and total IgG; IgG2a subtype response was higher than IgG1 in both groups.
Immune Response: Elevated IFN-γ and IL-10 levels observed in mice immunized with recombinant L. lactis; no change in IL-4 levels; indicating induction of both humoral and cellular immune responses.

Title:
Immunization efficacy and safety of Brucella 104M against aerosol challenge in BALB/c mice
Title: Immunization efficacy and safety of Brucella 104M against aerosol challenge in BALB/c mice
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the protective efficacy and safety of Brucella abortus strain 104M administered by intratracheal aerosol delivery, intranasal instillation, or subcutaneous injection in BALB/c mice.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 104M delivered via three routes: intratracheal aerosol, intranasal instillation, and subcutaneous injection.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Female BALB/c mice aged 6-8 weeks were immunized by the three routes. Clinical manifestations, body weight, spleen weight, bacterial loads in spleens, serum anti-Brucella antibody titers, and cytokine concentrations (IFN-γ, IL-18) in serum and lung homogenate were measured at 4, 8, 16, and 24 weeks post-immunization. At 22 weeks post-immunization, mice were challenged with Brucella A19 via intratracheal aerosol.
Vaccine Efficacy: Immunized mice showed no abnormal clinical symptoms or significant body weight changes. Spleen weights post-challenge were significantly lower in immunized groups compared to controls. Bacterial loads in spleens decreased over time and were significantly lower than controls after challenge. High titers of specific antibodies were detected, peaking at week 8. Cytokine levels (IFN-γ, IL-18) were elevated pre-challenge and modulated post-challenge. No significant differences were observed among immunization routes. The vaccine showed obvious protective efficacy against aerosol challenge.
Immune Response: Both humoral and cellular immunity were stimulated by the vaccine. High titers of Brucella 104M-specific IgG2a antibodies were detected, higher than IgG1. Cytokines IFN-γ, IL-18, and IL-1β concentrations in serum and lung homogenate were significantly elevated in immunized groups before challenge. After challenge, serum cytokine levels decreased compared to controls, while lung cytokine levels remained elevated.

Title: Evaluation of the immune responses against reduced doses of Brucella abortus S19 (calfhood) vaccine in water buffaloes (Bubalus bubalis), India

Title: Oral co-administration of bivalent protein r-BL with U-Omp19 elicits mucosal immune responses and reduces S. Typhimurium shedding in BALB/c mice
Standardized Vaccine Name: Salmonella Typhimurium sseB ompL and Brucella abortus U-Omp19 subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The fusion protein r-BL was constructed by splicing Salmonella Typhimurium sseB and ompL genes through a G4S linker by overlap extension PCR. It was orally co-administered with Brucella abortus U-Omp19 protein, which has known protease inhibitor activity.
Vaccine Formulation: Oral co-administration of the bivalent protein r-BL with the mucosal adjuvant U-Omp19.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of BALB/c mice followed by measurement of mucosal IgA, IgM, IgG1, and IgG2a antibody titers in fecal samples and intestinal washes; challenge study measuring fecal shedding of Salmonella Typhimurium.
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant increase in mucosal IgA titers in fecal samples and intestinal washes; increased mucosal IgM, IgG1, and IgG2a isotypes; significant reduction in fecal shedding of Salmonella Typhimurium; complete termination of Salmonella fecal shedding by day 12 post-challenge in treated mice.
Immune Response: Triggered mucosal immune responses including elevated mucosal IgA, IgM, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies, indicating activation of the mucosal arm of the immune system as the first line of defense against enteric Salmonella infection.

Vaccine Introduction: This study introduced recombinant Lactococcus lactis MG1363 expressing a fusion protein of Brucella melitensis Omp16 and human IL2 (rOmp16-IL2) as a candidate for a safe, non-pathogenic mucosal live vaccine against brucellosis.

Serum IgG levels were measured by indirect ELISA before and two weeks after the last immunization.

Immune Response: The vaccine induced a significant serum IgG antibody response in BALB/c mice, indicating immunogenicity of the rOmp16-IL2 fusion protein delivered by recombinant L. lactis or as purified protein with adjuvant.

Vaccine Efficacy: No differences were observed in cellular proliferation assay and serological tests to B. abortus between brucellosis vaccinated group and concomitant vaccinated group.
Immune Response: Vaccination induced an increase in rectal temperature for 3 days and local temperature for 7 days; no differences in immune response were observed between brucellosis only and concomitant vaccination groups.

Title: Design of a new multi-epitope vaccine against Brucella based on T and B cell epitopes using bioinformatics methods
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella Omp22 Omp19 Omp28 multi-epitope vaccine

Title: In Vitro Evaluation of Immunogenicity of Recombinant OMP25 Protein Obtained from Endemic Brucella abortus Biovar 3 as Vaccine Candidate Molecule Against Animal Brucellosis

Title: Mucosal Vaccination Primes NK Cell-Dependent Development of CD8(+) T Cells Against Pulmonary Brucella Infection
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain znBAZ live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The live, double-mutant B. abortus (znBAZ) strain was used for mucosal vaccination to induce protection against pulmonary challenge with wild-type Brucella.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Mice were nasally dosed with wt B. abortus, smooth vaccine strain 19 (S19), or znBAZ; flow cytometric analysis was performed to assess innate immune cell activation, NK cell frequency and activation, dendritic cell activation and migration, and CD8+ T cell induction.

Title: Immune Responses and Efficacy of Brucella Abortus Strain RB51 in Bison After Delivery in a Dry Dart Formulation or by Parenteral Inoculation
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was administered to bison heifer calves either by single or booster parenteral delivery or by surgical implantation of a dry dart formulation.
Vaccine Formulation: Live Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine delivered either parenterally or via a novel dry dart formulation.

Vaccine Efficacy: Parenteral vaccination, especially with booster, reduced abortions and infection in uterine and fetal tissues compared to controls; dry dart formulation reduced abortion but did not significantly reduce infection in tissues.
Immune Response: Parenteral vaccinates showed significantly greater serum humoral and PBMC proliferative responses to RB51 compared to controls; dry dart vaccinates had lower humoral responses and no significant proliferative response compared to controls.

Title:

Title: Natural Brucella melitensis Infection and Rev. 1 Vaccination Induce Specific Brucella O-Polysaccharide Antibodies Involved in Complement Mediated Brucella Cell Killing
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination against brucellosis using live attenuated strains is the primary approach in protecting livestock through a strong cellular immune response; Rev. 1 vaccination induces serum anti-Brucella antibodies mostly against Brucella O-polysaccharide.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 administered intraocularly.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Serum samples from Rev. 1 vaccinated sheep were tested for Brucella O-polysaccharide antibodies by complement fixation test, microplate agglutination test, and ELISA; serum bactericidal activity (SBA) assay was used to assess Brucella killing ability in vitro.
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant increase in serum bactericidal activity 30 days post-vaccination compared to pre-vaccination; sera containing Brucella O-polysaccharide IgG antibodies showed significantly higher killing ability against Brucella melitensis strains 16M and Rev. 1; convalescent sheep sera demonstrated significant killing ability against field strain 16M.
Immune Response: Rev. 1 vaccination induces specific Brucella O-polysaccharide IgG antibodies that participate in complement mediated Brucella killing in vitro, suggesting a potential protective role through this mechanism.

Title: Evaluation of the goat cellular immune response to rBtuB-Hia-FlgK peptides from Brucella melitensis
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella melitensis rBtuB Hia FlgK subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the goat Th1/Th2 immune response to a cocktail of three Brucella melitensis peptides (rBtuB-Hia-FlgK) previously shown to induce antigen-specific immune responses in rodent models.
Vaccine Formulation: A cocktail of three peptides (rBtuB, Hia, FlgK) from Brucella melitensis was used; adjuvant was included but not specified.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Twenty-eight goats were divided into four groups and immunized with the peptide cocktail, adjuvant alone, PBS, or the Rev-1 vaccine. Peripheral blood samples were collected on days 0, 15, and 80 post-inoculation. CD4+ and CD8+ T cell proliferation and cytokine production (Th1: IL-2, IL-12, TNF-α, IFN-γ; Th2: IL-4, IL-5, IL-10) were evaluated.
Vaccine Efficacy: The peptide cocktail induced an increase in CD4+/CD8+ T cells starting at day 15 and persisting to day 80. IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2 mRNA expression were induced by day 15, with IFN-γ levels maintained at day 80. Although IFN-γ production was lower than that induced by Rev-1 at day 15, this may be due to sampling timing.
Immune Response: The vaccine induced a Th1-type cellular immune response characterized by increased CD4+/CD8+ T cell proliferation and production of Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2), similar to the response induced by the live attenuated Rev-1 vaccine. The results suggest the peptide cocktail can induce cellular immunity comparable to an attenuated vaccine.

Title: Oral vaccination with novel Lactococcus lactis mucosal live vector-secreting Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) protein induces humoral and cellular immune protection against Brucella abortus

Title: Characterization of humoral and cellular immune responses elicited by reduced doses of Brucella abortus S19 (calfhood) vaccine in cattle calves of India
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella abortus S19 vaccine is a stable attenuated smooth strain, globally used as calfhood vaccine for prevention of bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Formulation: Four graded doses tested: full dose (40 × 10^9 CFU/dose), and reduced doses of 1/10th, 1/20th, and 1/100th of full dose.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Vaccination of 13 cattle calves (4-5 months old) per dose group; blood samples collected from 0 to 240 days post-vaccination at multiple intervals to assess innate, humoral, and cell-mediated immune responses.
Vaccine Efficacy: Sero-conversion observed in all vaccinated animals by day 45 post-vaccination with antibody persistence till day 240; no significant difference in antibody response between full dose and 1/10th reduced dose groups.
Immune Response: Dose-dependent innate and cell-mediated responses measured by IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γ, CD4+ and CD8+ cell counts; no significant difference between full dose and 1/10th reduced dose groups, suggesting comparable immune responses.

Title: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin-Trained Macrophages Elicit a Protective Inflammatory Response against the Pathogenic Bacteria Brucella abortus
Lab Model or Cell: Mus musculus (C57BL/6 mice); RAG-1-deficient mice; bone marrow-derived macrophages
Vaccine Introduction: The BCG vaccine is known to elicit enhanced innate immune responses (trained immunity) against a wide range of infections.

Gene or Protein Antigen: wbkC gene replaced by wbdR gene (modified O-polysaccharide)
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine candidate A19mut2 was developed by replacing the formyltransferase gene wbkC in Brucella abortus A19 with the acetyltransferase gene wbdR from E. coli O157, resulting in a modified O-polysaccharide that does not induce antibodies against wild-type Brucella LPS, enabling DIVA (Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals) capability.

Title:
Contrasting roles for IgM and B-cell MHCII expression in Brucella abortus S19 vaccine-mediated efficacy against B. melitensis infection
Title: Contrasting roles for IgM and B-cell MHCII expression in Brucella abortus S19 vaccine-mediated efficacy against B. melitensis infection
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immune mechanisms underlying the licensed live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine, which is commercially available for animals but not suitable for human use.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: In vivo B-cell depletion, immunodeficient and transgenic mouse models were used to study B-cell roles, antigen uptake and presentation, antibody production, and class switching in S19-mediated immunity against Brucella melitensis infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: S19 vaccination conferred protection against virulent Brucella melitensis infection. Antibody production, especially secretory IgM, was protective early after challenge. B-cell MHCII expression negatively impacted vaccine efficacy at later timepoints. B-cell depletion after vaccination but before challenge enhanced protection, indicating a deleterious role of B cells during the challenge phase. T follicular helper cell deficiency reduced vaccine efficacy at later stages independent of antibody production.
Immune Response: Protective immunity was associated with secretory IgM antibody production and complement activation early after challenge. T follicular helper cells influenced IgG production and vaccine efficacy at later stages through T-cell function rather than antibody production. B-cell MHCII expression had a negative effect on vaccine efficacy. B-cell depletion enhanced protection, suggesting complex and phase-dependent roles of B-cell effector functions in vaccine-mediated immunity.

Vaccine Introduction: The study describes the production of a highly soluble and immuno-reactive recombinant flagellin protein (rFliA(C)) of Clostridium chauvoei, a causative agent of blackleg affecting cattle and small ruminants worldwide. Title: Intranasal and intraperitoneal immunization against Brucella infection using niosome and mannosylated niosomes containing Brucella recombinant trigger factor/Bp26/Omp31 chimeric protein in a mouse model

Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella trigger factor BP26 Omp31 subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to evaluate immunity induced by a mannosylated niosome containing a recombinant chimeric protein composed of Brucella trigger factor, BP26, and Omp31 in a mouse model.

Cytokine production was significantly higher in vaccinated groups, especially with intraperitoneal administration, and immunization conferred protection against Brucella challenge.
Immune Response: The vaccine stimulated both cellular and humoral immune responses, with increased production of cytokines (IFN-gamma, IL-4, IL-12) and antibodies. The intraperitoneal route elicited stronger cytokine responses than the intranasal route.

Title: Immunogenicity of Brucella Trivalent Immunogen-Containing Polyethyleneimine Nanostructure Targeted with LPS in a Mouse Model
Make Vaccine Name: Brucella TF; BP26; omp31 subunit vaccine
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella TF BP26 omp31 subunit vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: A trivalent candidate antigen formulation containing TF, BP26, and omp31 was designed and evaluated using bioinformatics, cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21, purified, and incorporated into a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS to stimulate selective immune responses.
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant proteins encapsulated inside a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS; nanoparticle properties such as size, zeta potential, retention rate, diffusion efficacy, and antigen binding were characterized for injection and inhalation delivery in mice.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Mice were immunized on days 0, 10, 24, and 38 with different groups of antigens and nanoparticles; cytokine levels (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-12) in spleen cells and serum IgG1 and IgG2a antibody concentrations were measured two weeks after the last injection.
Vaccine Efficacy: Recombinant protein and nanoparticle formulations induced significant immune responses compared to controls and showed good response upon subsequent injections with live bacterial strains.
Immune Response: Significant production of IgG1, IgG2a, IFN-γ, IL-12, and IL-4 cytokines indicating stimulation of both cellular and humoral immunity compared to positive and negative control groups.

Title:
The instability of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 and a note on significance of using an unstable rough strain in the diagnosis of bovine brucellosis
Title: The instability of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 and a note on significance of using an unstable rough strain in the diagnosis of bovine brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine strain 45/20 was experimentally inoculated into heifers to study its immunogenicity and stability.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Experimental inoculation of six heifers with live Brucella abortus strain 45/20 and comparison with six bullocks inoculated with virulent Brucella abortus strain 544.
Vaccine Efficacy: The serum agglutinin titres in heifers inoculated with strain 45/20 were similar to those in bullocks inoculated with virulent strain 544, but the agglutinin response appeared more slowly and disappeared earlier in heifers.
Immune Response: The agglutinin response induced by strain 45/20 was slower in onset and shorter in duration compared to virulent strain 544; strain 45/20 is unstable and can revert to smooth form, becoming highly agglutinogenic in non-pregnant heifers.

Title:

Title: Transient enhancement of the serum antibody response to Brucella abortus strain 19 in cattle treated with levamisole

Title:
Effects of challenge dose on the clinical and immune responses of cattle vaccinated with reduced doses of Brucella abortus strain 19
Title: Effects of challenge dose on the clinical and immune responses of cattle vaccinated with reduced doses of Brucella abortus strain 19
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the protective efficacy of reduced doses (10^9 or 10^10 CFU) of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine in pregnant beef heifers.
Vaccine Formulation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine administered at reduced doses.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Pregnant beef heifers were vaccinated with reduced doses of strain 19 and then challenged intraconjunctivally with virulent B. abortus S2308 at two different doses (9.4 x 10^6 CFU and 5.2 x 10^7 CFU) in two separate experiments.
Vaccine Efficacy: In the lower challenge dose experiment, vaccination with strain 19 afforded significant protection against abortion or delivery of weak calves; in the higher challenge dose experiment, vaccination did not provide significant protection.
Immune Response: Vaccinated heifers showed significantly higher lymphocyte blast transformation assay responses compared to non-vaccinated heifers; serologic responses varied with challenge dose and vaccination status, with early serologic responses differing between experiments.

Title: Vaccination of ewes by a single conjunctival administration of Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated a single conjunctival vaccination of ewes with Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine at two doses (1.4 x 10^8 or 1.4 x 10^9 CFU) compared to subcutaneous vaccination (1.6 x 10^9 CFU).

Title: A BtpB-Deleted Brucella Vaccine Strain Provides Dual Advantages: Enhanced Protection and Diagnostic Differentiation Capability in Mice
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain A19 btpB deletion live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to reduce potential virulence, enhance protective efficacy, and enable differentiation from wild-type strains by knocking out the immunosuppressive virulence gene btpB in the A19 strain.

Title: Evaluation of the efficacy of polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 formulated in a new cage-like particle adjuvant (ISPA YOLK) administered by parenteral or mucosal routes against Brucella ovis in rams
Extracted Vaccine Name: polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 formulated in ISPA YOLK
Make Vaccine Name: polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 formulated in ISPA YOLK
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella ovis causes ram-contagious epididymitis, a major reproductive disorder in flocks. The attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 provides heterologous protection but has disadvantages. Subunit vaccines like polymeric BLSOmp31 offer a safer alternative aligned with One Health principles.
Vaccine Formulation: The vaccine consists of polymeric BLSOmp31 antigen formulated with a new low-cost cage-like particle adjuvant variant called ISPA YOLK.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: The vaccine was administered to rams via subcutaneous and ocular (mucosal) routes. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were evaluated, along with protective efficacy against experimental Brucella ovis infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: The vaccine did not prevent experimental infection but parenterally immunized rams showed fewer infected organs and less severe histopathological lesions in reproductive organs compared to ocularly vaccinated and non-immunized rams. Both administration routes reduced Brucella ovis elimination through semen, potentially lowering infection spread.
Immune Response: Vaccination induced systemic and variable mucosal IgG and IgA antibody responses without interfering with serological diagnosis. It also elicited significant specific cellular immune responses and increased cytokine gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells, showing a mixed Th1/Th2 profile.

Vaccine Introduction: The study addresses the challenge of differentiating infected from vaccinated animals (DIVA) and false positives in diagnostics based on Brucella lipopolysaccharide. Vaccine Formulation: Spacer-armed di-, tri-, tetra-, and penta-4,6-dideoxy-4-formamido-α-(1→2)-d-mannopyranosides were synthesized using orthogonal glycosylation strategies, sequential block-wise assembly, deprotection, and conversion into fluorescein-labeled conjugates.

Immune Response: The assay detected anti-Brucella immunoglobulins, demonstrating the immunological relevance of the synthetic oligosaccharide conjugates as tracers for antibody detection.

Title: Post-vaccination sero-monitoring of bovine calves in Indian subcontinent: A review on progress towards brucellosis control
Vaccine Introduction: India has implemented nationwide S19 vaccination in cattle and buffaloes to control brucellosis.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Multi-phase sero-monitoring study analyzing 19,893 serum samples from cattle and buffalo calves aged 4-8 months collected during 2021-2024 across five Indian states/union territories; samples tested using laboratory standardized indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (iELISA).
Vaccine Efficacy: Overall sero-conversion rates were 75.87% in cattle and 67.22% in buffaloes, with significant species-specific disparities; regional variation observed with Tamil Nadu achieving up to 84.61% overall and some districts 100% sero-conversion; other regions showed lower rates especially in buffaloes; Odisha showed phase-wise improvement in buffalo calves from 17.64% to 57.5%.
Immune Response: Measured by sero-conversion rates using iELISA indicating immune response post-vaccination; species-specific differences noted with cattle showing higher sero-conversion than buffaloes.

Title: Assessment of immune responses to Brucella abortus S19 vaccination in cattle and buffaloes
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine

Title: OMP16-targeting monoclonal antibodies H4 and E6 reveal essential linear epitopes for Brucella immunoprotection

Title:
The Brucella abortus A19ΔfeuPΔfeuQ double-mutant is highly attenuated and confers protection in BALB/c mice
Title: The Brucella abortus A19ΔfeuPΔfeuQ double-mutant is highly attenuated and confers protection in BALB/c mice
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain A19 delta feuP delta feuQ live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Type: VO:0000350: live virulent vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study addresses limitations of the current Brucella abortus A19 vaccine, including residual virulence and inability to differentiate infected from vaccinated animals. A double-gene deletion mutant (A19ΔfeuPΔfeuQ) was constructed by removing genes encoding a two-component regulatory system (TCS) on chromosome II to improve safety and diagnostic compatibility.
Vaccine Formulation: A live attenuated double-gene deletion mutant derived from Brucella abortus strain A19 with deletions in feuP and feuQ genes.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Intracellular survival assays and vaccination-challenge experiments were performed in BALB/c mice to assess attenuation, immune response, and protective efficacy. Serological assays were used to evaluate differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals.
Vaccine Efficacy: The A19ΔfeuPΔfeuQ mutant showed a greater than 1.5-log reduction in intracellular survival and a 2.34-log greater reduction in bacterial burden at 4 weeks post-challenge compared to controls, indicating marked attenuation and effective protection.
Immune Response: Vaccination induced significantly higher titers of IgG antibodies. The FEUP and FEUQ proteins served as specific antigens enabling serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated animals.
