Title: Evaluation of Humoral and Cellular Immune Responses to the Conjunctival Brucella abortus S19 Vaccine in Türkiye
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine is administered via the conjunctival route to control bovine brucellosis in Türkiye.
Vaccine Formulation: Locally produced Brucella abortus S19 vaccine used for conjunctival vaccination.

Title: Brucella-infected macrophage-derived microparticles enhance the host anti-Brucella acquired immune response
Lab Model or Cell: Mus musculus; RAW264.7 macrophages; bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs)
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates microparticles (MPs) released from macrophages infected with the attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5, exploring their role in enhancing host defense and adaptive immunity against Brucella.
Vaccine Formulation: Microparticles derived from macrophages infected with Brucella melitensis strain M5.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: In vitro infection of RAW264.7 macrophages to generate MPs; murine models to assess immune response; activation assays on bone marrow-derived dendritic cells; cytotoxic T lymphocyte priming and target lysis assays.

Immune Response: Th1-polarized immunity characterized by increased IgG2a titers and IFN-γ production; activation of NF-κB pathway in dendritic cells; increased IL-12 and TNF-α secretion; priming of cytotoxic T lymphocytes via direct and indirect pathways.

Title: Impact of inactivation methods on biosafety and antigen reactivity of Brucella melitensis from the perspective of Astral-DIA proteomics based on antibody immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated inactivation methods for the Brucella melitensis Rev.1 vaccine strain to ensure biosafety and preserve antigen reactivity for vaccine development and diagnostics.
Vaccine Formulation: The Rev.1 strain was subjected to heat inactivation (80°C/95°C for 10-20 min) and formaldehyde inactivation (0.4%/0.6% for 48-72 h) to assess effects on antigen preservation.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Antibody immunoprecipitation-based Orbitrap Astral DIA proteomics, ELISA, and Western Blot analyses were used to evaluate protein detectability and immunoreactivity after inactivation.
Vaccine Efficacy: Complete inactivation of Rev.1 was achieved by heating at 80°C/95°C for 20 min or 0.6% formaldehyde for 48-72 h, with superior immunoreactivity compared to phenol inactivation.
Immune Response: Formaldehyde treatment for 48 h preserved soluble antigens and epitopes better, while heat inactivation enhanced immunoreactivity of membrane and stress proteins, indicating suitability for targeted epitope studies.

Vaccine Introduction:
The study evaluated inactivation methods for the Brucella melitensis Rev.1 vaccine strain to ensure biosafety and preserve antigen reactivity for vaccine development and diagnostics.

Vaccine Formulation:
The Rev.1 strain was subjected to heat inactivation (80°C/95°C for 10-20 min) and formaldehyde inactivation (0.4%/0.6% for 48-72 h) to assess effects on antigen preservation.

Experiment Used to investigate the vaccine:
Antibody immunoprecipitation-based Orbitrap Astral DIA proteomics, ELISA, and Western Blot analyses were used to evaluate protein detectability and immunoreactivity after inactivation.

Complete inactivation of Rev.1 was achieved by heating at 80°C/95°C for 20 min or 0.6% formaldehyde for 48-72 h, with superior immunoreactivity compared to phenol inactivation.

Immune Response:
Formaldehyde treatment for 48 h preserved soluble antigens and epitopes better, while heat inactivation enhanced immunoreactivity of membrane and stress proteins, indicating suitability for targeted epitope studies.

Title: Upregulation of innate and adaptive immune mechanisms facilitating prevention of gastric Helicobacter pylori infection in guinea pigs by per os administration of chitosan microparticles loaded with Mycobacterium bovis BCG

Title:
An Immunoinformatics-Guided Multi-Epitope Vaccine Targeting the WbkC Protein Confers Protection Against Brucella Challenge in BALB/c Mice
Title: An Immunoinformatics-Guided Multi-Epitope Vaccine Targeting the WbkC Protein Confers Protection Against Brucella Challenge in BALB/c Mice
Vaccine Introduction: A novel multi-epitope vaccine was designed using immunoinformatics methods targeting the WbkC protein, a methyltransferase involved in O-antigen biosynthesis of Brucella lipopolysaccharide, known to stimulate strong immune responses in mice.
Vaccine Formulation: Immunodominant linear B lymphocyte, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and helper T lymphocyte epitopes of WbkC were linked with short connectors to construct the recombinant protein rWbkC; bioinformatics predicted high antigenicity, solubility, and no allergenicity or toxicity; molecular docking showed stable binding to TLR2/4.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: In vivo immunization of BALB/c mice with three doses of rWbkC; immune simulation analyses; bacterial challenge with Brucella melitensis M5 strain; measurement of antibody levels (IgG, IgG1) and bacterial loads in spleen and liver.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination with rWbkC significantly reduced bacterial loads in spleen and liver compared to PBS control (p < 0.001); rWbkC showed superior clearance of bacterial burden in liver compared to WbkC protein alone (p < 0.01).
Immune Response: rWbkC induced significantly higher IgG and IgG1 antibody levels than WbkC protein; immune simulation predicted elevated IFN-γ, IL-2, and IgG/IgM levels, indicating strong cellular and humoral immune responses.

Title: Evaluation of lymphocyte blastogenesis for diagnosis of bovine brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine strain 19 was used to vaccinate pregnant heifers to evaluate lymphocyte blastogenesis responses.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Peripheral blood lymphocytes from vaccinated cattle were tested with purified Brucella abortus porin proteins and Brucella abortus soluble antigen (BASA) in a lymphocyte blastogenesis test (LBT) measuring blastogenic response over a range of cell concentrations.
Vaccine Efficacy: Pregnant heifers vaccinated with strain 19 could generally be distinguished from pregnant animals infected with virulent strain 2308 by LBT responses to porin; however, some nonpregnant infected heifers showed inconsistent or no response.
Immune Response: LBT responses to porin proteins showed differences between vaccinated and infected animals; false positive responses occurred less frequently with porin than with BASA; high circulating agglutinins were associated with lack of LBT responsiveness; purified Brucella LPS did not induce false positive mitogenic responses.

Title: Immune response to porin in cattle immunized with whole cell, outer membrane, and outer membrane protein antigens of Brucella abortus combined with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants
Make Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus porin; outer membrane proteins; outer membrane; whole cell (rough strain 45/20) inactivated vaccine
Standardized Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 outer membrane protein inactivated vaccine
Adjuvant: yes; trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide (N-acetylmuramyl-L-alpha-aminobutyryl-D-isoglutamine)
Gene or Protein Antigen: porin; outer membrane proteins; outer membrane; whole cell (rough strain 45/20)
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated nonliving vaccines derived from Brucella abortus rough strain 45/20 containing porin and other outer membrane protein antigens combined with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants.
Vaccine Formulation: Vaccines contained trehalose dimycolate and a derivative of muramyl dipeptide at fixed doses; antigen types included whole cell, outer membrane, and detergent-extracted outer membrane proteins; mineral oil quantity was varied.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Factorial experiment testing antigen type, antigen quantity, and mineral oil quantity on immune response; blastogenesis and antibody titers measured over 10 weeks; delayed-type hypersensitivity assessed by intradermal injection.

Immune Response: Strong blastogenesis responses to porin, highest antibody titers to porin-lipopolysaccharide complex with outer membrane proteins; delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions observed; immune responses exceeded those after natural or experimental infection.

Title:
Opposite effects of total lymphoid irradiation on T cell-dependent and T cell-independent antibody responses
Title: Opposite effects of total lymphoid irradiation on T cell-dependent and T cell-independent antibody responses
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigated the effect of total lymphoid irradiation (TLI) on the primary antibody response to Brucella abortus trinitrophenylated polysaccharide antigen (TNP-BA).
Vaccine Formulation: The antigen was trinitrophenylated polysaccharide from Brucella abortus; adjuvant used was complete Freund's adjuvant for the other antigen but not specified for TNP-BA.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Immunization of BALB/c mice with TNP-BA antigen after total lymphoid irradiation at different time points; antibody responses measured.
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody response to TNP-BA was diminished when immunized within 3 days after TLI but enhanced 5- to 10-fold when immunized 30 days after TLI compared to controls.
Immune Response: Total lymphoid irradiation had opposite effects on T cell-dependent and T cell-independent antibody responses; specifically, T cell-independent antibody response to TNP-BA was enhanced after recovery from TLI.

Title:
An evaluation of the anamnestic test for brucellosis in cattle of the northern pastoral area
Title: An evaluation of the anamnestic test for brucellosis in cattle of the northern pastoral area
Vaccine Introduction: The vaccine was used to investigate the anamnestic test for brucellosis in weaner cattle on two farms in western Queensland.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Groups of about 500 weaner cattle were bled before and at 6 or 10 weeks after vaccination and again the following year; serums were tested by complement fixation test (CFT), Rose Bengal test (RBT), and indirect haemolysis test (IHLT); bacteriological examination was performed on selected tissues from cattle reacting to one or more tests.
Vaccine Efficacy: B. abortus was isolated from 24% of cattle reacting at 6 or 10 weeks after vaccination; the vaccine induced serological responses detectable by CFT, RBT, and IHLT; the CFT was the most efficient test for detecting infected animals.
Immune Response: The vaccine induced serological responses measurable by CFT, RBT, and IHLT; CFT showed higher sensitivity in detecting infected animals both pre-vaccination and post-vaccination; interpretation of CFT titres following 45/20 vaccination requires re-examination.

Vaccine Introduction: Mice vaccinated with a protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan Brucella fraction produced immune sera that completely stopped dissemination of Brucella abortus 544 infection to the spleen.
Vaccine Formulation: Protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fraction of Brucella used to generate immune serum.

Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to modify strain 19 calfhood vaccination to eliminate persistent serological reactions interfering with eradication programs and to find an effective vaccination method applicable to all ages of cattle, allowing calfhood vaccination to be safely stopped.
Vaccine Formulation: Reduced dose levels of strain 19 were tested, including a booster dose given conjunctivally one year after initial vaccination at 1 month of age; doses included 6 x 10^9 c.f.u. and 3 x 10^8 c.f.u.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Four summarized experiments involving vaccination of calves at 1 month, booster vaccination, vaccination of pregnant cows with reduced doses, and vaccination of mature non-pregnant heifers with reduced doses.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccination at 1 month followed by a reduced dose booster induced immunity at least equal to conventional calfhood vaccination; vaccination of pregnant cows with reduced doses gave better immunity than calfhood vaccination; vaccination of mature non-pregnant heifers with reduced dose produced immunity at least as good as calfhood vaccination.

Vaccinal immune status of mice was reflected by the number of bacteria in spleens after challenge, indicating the vaccine induced measurable immunity.

Title: Leukocyte migration-inhibition responses of nonvaccinated and vaccinated heifers to experimental infection with Brucella abortus
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccinated heifers were experimentally infected with Brucella abortus to assess leukocyte migration-inhibition responses.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Leukocyte migration agarose technique was used to measure leukocyte migration-inhibition responses in vaccinated and nonvaccinated heifers after exposure to Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: None of the vaccinated heifers aborted, whereas nonvaccinated heifers had abortions; vaccinated heifers showed significantly lower leukocyte migration-inhibition responses compared to nonvaccinated heifers.

Title:
Persistence of Brucella abortus strain 19 infection in adult cattle vaccinated with reduced doses
Title: Persistence of Brucella abortus strain 19 infection in adult cattle vaccinated with reduced doses
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigated the persistence of Brucella abortus strain 19 infection in adult cattle vaccinated with reduced doses of the vaccine.
Vaccine Formulation: Reduced doses of viable Brucella abortus strain 19 cells were used, specifically doses of 5.8 x 10^9, 2.8 x 10^8, and 3 x 10^8 viable cells.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Necropsy and isolation of strain 19 from vaccinated cows at three to six months post-vaccination; serological testing of vaccinated cows; observation of pregnancy outcomes including abortion and premature calving.
Vaccine Efficacy: The lower dose of 3 x 10^8 viable cells produced immunity equal to that of higher doses and did not interfere with pregnancy in over 700 cattle; however, higher doses led to colonization and adverse pregnancy outcomes in some cows.
Immune Response: Serological positivity was observed approximately three months after vaccination in cows vaccinated with the lower dose.

Title:
Determination of the optimal inoculation dose of Brucella chemical vaccine
Title: Determination of the optimal inoculation dose of Brucella chemical vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study aimed to determine the optimal inoculation dose of the Brucella chemical vaccine.
Vaccine Formulation: Chemical vaccine administered intramuscularly at doses ranging from 0.5 mg to 2 mg.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Evaluation of reactogenicity, antigenic and immunogenic activity at four different doses in subjects, measuring seroconversion frequency, agglutinin titers, and persistence using Wright's agglutination test and Huddleson's test.
Vaccine Efficacy: The 1 mg dose produced the highest percentage of seroconversions, highest agglutinin titers, and longest persistence of antibodies among the tested doses.
Immune Response: Vaccination induced seroconversion with high agglutinin titers; no pronounced sensitization was observed even at doses up to 2 mg; seroconversion frequency correlated well between Wright's and Huddleson's tests.

Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route. I.--Protection demonstrated in guinea pigs

Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route
Vaccine Type: VO:0000504: whole organism vaccine; VO:0010038: live attenuated vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated vaccination of cattle with low doses of Brucella abortus strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route compared to subcutaneous injection of formalin-killed bacteria.
Vaccine Formulation: Live bacteria doses ranging from 10^6 to 10^10 CFU administered conjunctivally; formalin-killed bacteria (2.5 to 5 x 10^10) administered subcutaneously.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Vaccination of 25-month-old cows and 4-month-old calves with various doses of live or killed Brucella abortus strain 19; serological testing (agglutination, complement fixation, Coombs, Rose Bengal) and lymph node culture post-mortem.
Vaccine Efficacy: Colonization of regional lymph nodes was observed consistently at doses of 5 x 10^9 and 10^10 live bacteria; low or no significant serological response was induced at these doses; the 5 x 10^9 dose was identified as most suitable for vaccination due to consistent colonization without significant serological response.
Immune Response: Low but definite agglutination titers observed only at highest dose (10^10) in cows; serological responses were rare in calves and limited to agglutination and Coombs tests; complement fixation tests were negative in all sera.

Title:

Title: Effects of Concanavalin A, fed as a constituent of Jack bean (Canavalia ensiformis L.) seeds, on the humoral immune response and performance of broiler chickens
Vaccine Introduction: Chicks were immunized against Brucella abortus at 5 weeks of age to evaluate antibody response.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Antibody titers against Brucella abortus were measured by ELISA one week after immunization in broiler chickens fed diets containing raw or toasted Jack bean seeds with Concanavalin A.

Title: Evaluation of serologic responses, lymphocyte proliferative responses, and clearance from lymphatic organs after vaccination of bison with Brucella abortus strain RB51

Title:
Vaccination against bovine brucellosis with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route. III. -- Serological response and immunity in the pregnant cow
Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route. III. -- Serological response and immunity in the pregnant cow
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated vaccination of heifers with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route, comparing it to standard subcutaneous vaccination and combinations thereof.
Vaccine Formulation: Vaccination was performed using 9 x 10^10 bacteria subcutaneously or 5 x 10^9 bacteria by the conjunctival route, with some groups receiving booster vaccinations by the conjunctival route.
Experiment Used to investigate the vacci: Seventy-four heifers were randomized into four groups with different vaccination regimens; serological tests (agglutination, complement fixation, Rose Bengal), challenge with B. abortus strain 544 during pregnancy, bacteriological examination of various tissues and fluids, and bacterial enumeration at slaughter were performed.
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccinated groups showed significantly lower infection levels compared to controls; groups receiving conjunctival booster vaccinations (groups C and D) had better protection than standard subcutaneous vaccination alone (group B); two conjunctival vaccinations were at least as effective as the standard system.
Immune Response: Serological responses varied by vaccination route; standard subcutaneous vaccination induced typical serological responses; conjunctival vaccination induced lower and shorter-lasting titers; booster conjunctival vaccination caused a transient rise in titers lasting about 3 months.
